source_text:
Προδήλων οὖν ἡμῖν ὄντων τούτων, καὶ ἐγκεκυφότες εἰς τὰ βάθη τῆς θείας γνώσεως. πάντα τάξει ποιεῖν ὀφείλομεν, ὅσα ὁ δεσπότης ἐπιτελεῖν ἐκέλευσεν κατὰ καιροὺς τεταγμένους.
τάς τε προσφορὰς καὶ λειτουργίας ἐπιτελεῖσθαι, καὶ οὐκ εἰκῆ ἢ ἀτάκτως ἐκέλευσεν γίνεσθαι, ἀλλ’ ὡρισμένοις καιροῖς καὶ ὥραις.
ποῦ τε καὶ διὰ τίνων ἐπιτελεῖσθαι θέλει, αὐτὸς ὥρισεν τῇ ὑπερτάτῳ αὐτοῦ βουλήσει. ἵν’ ὁσίως πάντα γινόμενα ἐν εὐδοκήσει εὐπρόσδεκτα εἴη τῷ θελήματι αὐτοῦ.
οἱ οὖν τοῖς προστεταγμένοις καιροῖς ποιοῦντες τὰς προσφορὰς αὐτῶν εὐπρόσδεκτοί τε καὶ μακάριοι: τοῖς γὰρ νομίμοις τοῦ δεσπότου ἀκολουθοῦντες οὐ διαμαρτάνουσιν.
τῷ γὰρ ἀρχιερεῖ ἴδιαι λειτουργίαι δεδομέναι εἰσίν, καὶ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν ἴδιος ὁ τόπος προστέτακται, καὶ Λευΐταις ἴδιαι διακονίαι ἐπίκεινται: ὁ λαϊκὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῖς λαῖκοῖς προστάγμασιν δέδεται.
orientation: The Roman church is explaining that God has fixed the times, places, and persons for worship, and that the Corinthians must follow this order.
pass_a_gloss: These things therefore [being] clear to us, and [we] having peered into the depths of the divine knowledge, all things in order we ought to do, as many as the master commanded to complete at appointed times. Both the offerings and ministries to be completed, and not at random or disorderly he commanded [them] to happen, but at defined times and hours. Where and through whom [they] are to be completed he wishes, he himself defined by his highest will. So that all things being done holily in good pleasure acceptable [they] might be to his will. Those therefore at the commanded times making their offerings acceptable and blessed [are]; for the lawful [commands] of the master following [they] do not err. For to the high priest own ministries have been given, and to the priests own the place has been assigned, and to Levites own services are laid upon [them]; the lay person to the lay commands is bound.

choices.why: The glossary fixes λειτουργία as 'ministry'; the plural here refers to the distinct liturgical services assigned to different orders.
The pair contrasts two failures of order: without purpose and without arrangement; keeping both adverbs distinct preserves the rhetorical force.
καιροῖς and ὥραις are near-synonyms; 'times and hours' keeps the distinction between seasons and specific hours of worship.
The phrase echoes divine approval; 'good pleasure' preserves the noun's sense of God's favorable will rather than flattening it to an adverb.
The phrase marks a category of person distinct from priests and Levites; 'lay person' keeps the technical sense without archaism.
The perfect participle carries the sense of a standing command; 'commanded' preserves the verbal force better than 'appointed.'

pass_b_english: Since these things are clear to us, and we have looked deeply into the knowledge of God, we must do everything in order, whatever the Lord commanded us to carry out at appointed times.
He commanded that the offerings and ministries be carried out, and not at random or in disorder, but at fixed times and hours.
Where and through whom he wishes them to be carried out, he himself determined by his supreme will, so that everything done in holiness would be acceptable to his will and pleasing to him.
Those who make their offerings at the commanded times are therefore acceptable and blessed, for they follow the Lord's lawful commands and do not go astray.

For to the high priest his own ministries have been given, and to the priests their own place has been assigned, and to the Levites their own services are laid upon them. The lay person is bound by the commands for the laity.

polish.changed: Clarified sentence flow and pronoun references, replaced awkward phrases like 'in good pleasure' and 'lay commands' with natural modern equivalents, and made the sequence of thought easier to follow aloud.

problems.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
problems.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.

edits.old: whatever the Master commanded us to carry out
edits.new: whatever the Lord commanded us to carry out

fixed: Standardized 'Master' to 'Lord' for God in both instances to maintain consistency with the work brief's divine title conventions.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'ministry' for λειτουργία; 'ministries' is plural but same term.
last_rejected.fix: For to the high priest his own ministries have been given
last_rejected.ruling: λειτουργίας is plural of λειτουργία; 'ministries' is the standard plural rendering, consistent with glossary entry.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'deacons' for διάκονοι and 'ministry' for λειτουργία; διακονία here is related service, but 'services' obscures the technical ministry terminology.
last_rejected.fix: and to the Levites their own ministries are laid upon them
last_rejected.ruling: διακονίαι means 'services'; rendering as 'services' is within normal range and not misleading in context.

last_rejected.quote: so that everything done in holiness would be acceptable to his will and pleasing to him
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵν’ ὁσίως πάντα γινόμενα ἐν εὐδοκήσει εὐπρόσδεκτα εἴη τῷ θελήματι αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: ἐν εὐδοκήσει (done in his good pleasure) is dropped, and “pleasing to him” is added as a second result of εὐπρόσδεκτα.
last_rejected.fix: so that everything done in holiness and in his good pleasure might be acceptable to his will.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐν εὐδοκήσει is rendered by "pleasing to him", a minor rephrasing; the sense (done in good pleasure, acceptable to his will) is preserved and no doctrine changes.
